messages:
maya: Thinking out loud — proposal to add a 'shadow exec' mode to the policy engine. Policy decisions would be evaluated in parallel (no-impact) and emitted to telemetry so we can compare live vs candidate strategies without changing traffic.

oliver: +1. how do you see this different from our existing canary/bake flows?

maya: Canary changes the live decision path for a subset of requests. Shadow exec keeps the live path untouched and runs the candidate path side-by-side for the same request, emitting a verdict record. We can measure disagreement rate, cost delta, latency delta, and fallback patterns.

priya: Biggest risk I see is KV-cache behavior — candidate path may warm caches that the live path won't see. That could bias latency results.

maya: Good call. Plan is to tag shadow requests and disable any cache population side-effects for shadow runs (read-only cache access). We still capture expected cache hits/misses so we can model warmed vs cold.

oliver: What about resource overhead? Running two policy evals per request doubles CPU for that component. Might blow up on hot paths.

maya: We should sample. Start with 1% of requests across a few representative routes, focus on lower-QPS tenants first. Also allow running only the policy-eval portion without calling downstream components (runtime routing) to keep overhead small.

anya: For metrics, I want a single disagreement metric that classifies by cause: latency_vs_cost_tradeoff, geo_mismatch, tier_mismatch, capacity_unavailable, compatibility. That will make triage easier.

maya: Agreed — proposed schema: verdict:{live_route, shadow_route, reason_code, decision_latency_ms, estimated_cost_delta, route_tags}. We'll emit to tracing and to a dedicated "policy-shadow" metrics stream.

infra-bot: deploy-bot started canary: policy-shadow-infra v0.1 -> infra-stage (no traffic).

priya: Privacy and Private deployments — shadowing in customer-managed runtimes could leak policy logic if we ship full traces. We need a config flag to redact tenant IDs or run only aggregated metrics for private mode.

oliver: Also consider model-variant compatibility. If the shadow picks a model that the runtime doesn't have locaux for, simulated cost may be wrong. We should include a compatibility check and mark those verdicts as 'incomplete'.

maya: Good. I'll add compatibility check and a field 'inference_compat' with values {OK, MISSING_VARIANT, REGION_RESTRICTED}.

anya: For rollout, propose phases: 1) local dev mode (no telemetry export), 2) internal staging sample 0.1% with full traces, 3) broader 1% + aggregated dashboards, 4) 5–10% only after low disagreement. Each phase gated by automated regression thresholds.

priya: How do we prevent shadow exec from affecting quotas or billing calculations?

maya: Shadow runs will never touch billing counters; their cost estimates are purely simulated. We'll flag them so downstream aggregators ignore those records for quota/billing.

oliver: Implementation detail: where in the stack? Policy service or upstream request router?

maya: Prefer inside the policy service so we can instrument decision internals. Minimal changes to router. Also allows plugging in different policy compilers for shadow runs.

anya: One more: correlate root trace id to shadow verdicts. Without correlation it's a pain to debug.

maya: Absolutely. We'll include trace_id and decision_id in the verdict record. Example log line:```json
{
  "trace_id": "abc123",
  "decision_id": "d-42",
  "live_route": "r-us-east-1/a",
  "shadow_route": "r-us-west-2/b",
  "reason_code": "latency_vs_cost_tradeoff",
  "decision_latency_ms": 2,
  "estimated_cost_delta": 0.0008
}
```

infra-bot: infra note: ensure BPF limits for policy pods are adjusted for shadow CPU spikes in staging.

priya: OK — I'll write a short RFC doc with config knobs, sampling, privacy controls, and metric names. Maya, can you capture the telemetry schema and decision log spec?

maya: On it. I'll open a docs PR and link to this thread. Thanks all. :rocket:
